drafted_from: tool row in tools/compare-voice-and-music-models/tool-rows.json, do-work/read_back_check.py and test/test_read_back_check.py
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check that the words heard back from line.wav read back every word of my script in line.txt."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it takes one script line and the words a Whisper model heard from its clip, and prints whether every word reads back in order.
instructions: 1. Hear the clip with tool:hear-sources and keep its answer as heard.json (the list of words it returned).
2. Say the check in start_here. Your AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:check-a-spoken-line-reads-back"} and runs the command in run with the script line and heard.json.
3. Read the result: ok true means every script word was heard back in order; missing lists the words that were not.

worked_examples.title: One spoken line checked against its script
worked_examples.ask: Did every word of my line read back?
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/compare-voice-and-music-models/do-work/read_back_check.py. Run: python3 -I tools/compare-voice-and-music-models/do-work/read_back_check.py "watch it slowed down." heard.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result":{"ok":false,"script_words":4,"missing":["slowed"]}}: a missing word fails the line; extra heard words do not. An unreadable heard file answers {"error": "..."}.
